Title: Halos Around Headlights at Night? Here's What Actually Slows Cataracts Down

Description:
Cataracts are the leading cause of vision impairment worldwide, and by 2020 an estimated 30 million Americans were living with one. Beyond blurry vision, watch for trouble seeing at night, glare sensitivity, halos around lights, faded colors, and needing new glasses more often.

Diabetes and high blood pressure accelerate how fast lens proteins break down, UV exposure adds free-radical damage over time, and smoking, heavy alcohol use, and long-term steroid medication add oxidative stress. Note: research hasn't shown lutein/zeaxanthin supplements lower cataract risk on their own — whole-food antioxidants like leafy greens and citrus are what the evidence actually supports.

Manage your blood sugar and blood pressure, wear UV400 sunglasses, and cut back on smoking and alcohol.

See an eye doctor right away if your vision clouds suddenly or you start seeing double in one eye.
